Subject: Schedule A pricing exhibit — question on billing-margin allocation

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the draft Order Form / Schedule A and had a few flagged items from our procurement and finance teams before we send this over to legal for redlines. The main item is the paragraph in Schedule A that references a "billing margin allocation" and a "safety buffer." The language as written is a bit open-ended and our finance team is concerned it could permit unilateral charge allocation in high-usage months without a clear cap or allocation methodology.

Can you confirm the intended mechanics? Specifically:
- Is the "billing margin" applied as an additive surcharge or as a reallocation of committed units?
- Is the "safety buffer" intended to be a temporary reserve that Redwood can draw against, and if so, what is the maximum percentage of monthly invoice it can represent?

Our preference is to have a numeric cap and a simple allocation formula included in the exhibit (e.g., max 12% of invoice, only applied to sustained >150% month-over-month usage for two consecutive months). If you can share a proposed tracked redline for Schedule A, that would help legal speed review.

Happy to hop on a 30-min call if that makes it faster.

Regards,

Hi Anya, Michael —

Thanks for raising this. Below is proposed exhibit language intended to replace the current ambiguous paragraph. We kept the mechanics simple and included both a cap and a notice/appeal process so there is predictability and remediation for customers.

[Proposed replacement text for Schedule A, Pricing Exhibit — Billing Margin & Safety Buffer]
1) Definitions. For purposes of this Exhibit, "Billing Margin" means the incremental invoice amount attributable to usage above the Customer's committed monthly units. "Safety Buffer" means a temporary reserve applied to a given invoice to cover short-term usage variance.

2) Application. The Safety Buffer may only be applied when a Customer's measured usage for a billing month exceeds 150% of the Customer's committed monthly units and such overage persists for two (2) consecutive billing months.

3) Cap. The Safety Buffer shall not exceed twelve percent (12%) of the invoice amount for any billing month. No single Safety Buffer application will exceed the lesser of (i) 12% of that month's invoice or (ii) the amount necessary to cover the usage overage above 150% of committed units.

4) Notice, Reporting & Appeal. Redwood will provide Customer written notice (email acceptable) within five (5) business days of applying a Safety Buffer. Such notice will include a usage report and calculation worksheet. Customer may dispute the Safety Buffer within twenty (20) business days and provide evidence; Redwood shall not collect disputed amounts while the dispute is under review unless Customer has prior credit arrangements.

5) True-up & Mitigation. If a Safety Buffer is applied in error, Redwood will credit the Customer on the next invoice (or sooner at Customer's request). For recurring sustained usage growth, both parties will engage in a good-faith account review to determine appropriate commit adjustments.

6) Operational Transparency. Redwood will share a monthly usage export and the calculation workbook (CSV) used to compute any Safety Buffer application.

Rationale: The 150%/2-month trigger plus a 12% cap is meant to balance Redwood's need to cover transient consumption spikes while protecting the customer from sudden open-ended charges. The notice and dispute window gives StellaMed an opportunity to review telemetry and escalate.

If StellaMed prefers a lower cap or a 60-day notice instead of 20 business days, we can discuss tradeoffs (e.g., reduce cap to 8% in exchange for longer notice).

I've attached the tracked PDF redline and the annotated Sched A workbook (same files Michael attached). Please confirm whether this maps to your procurement team's expectations and whether we should add a paragraph tying the Safety Buffer to specific invoice line codes for clarity.

-Laura
